content.text:
I fixed the SSRF issue with a one-line change in `lib/adapters/http.js:232`. The Node adapter no longer resolves URLs against `http://localhost`:

```js
const parsed = new URL(fullPath, platform.hasBrowserEnv ? platform.origin : undefined);
```

On a server there is no fallback base any more. A protocol-relative URL like `//google.com`, which skips `baseURL`, now fails with `ERR_INVALID_URL` ("Invalid URL") instead of being quietly turned into `http://google.com/`. That is the behaviour before 1.3.2, which is what the issue asks for. I checked it with a small script: `axios.create({baseURL}).get('//google.com')` now rejects with that error. In a browser environment, URLs still resolve against the page origin as before.

**Side effect:** on the server, a relative URL with no `baseURL` (for example `axios.get('/foo')`) also throws "Invalid URL" now. The 1.3.2 change (#5458) had made those resolve to `localhost`. That fallback is exactly what made the attack possible, so I removed it, but callers relying on it will need to set a `baseURL`.

**Tests:** `test/unit/adapters/http.js` gives the same result with and without my change: 109 passing, 2 failing. The two failures happen on the unmodified code too; one of them is the rate-limit download test hitting its 2000ms timeout. I didn't add a regression test because existing tests weren't to be modified.
